evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.3.53: homō gnāvus et industrius (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of people who get on with the work: busy, diligent, active (Lewis & Short). Its noun nāvitās and adverb nāviter follow.

terms.gloss: short, quick (of a way or method)
evidence: Cic. Off. 2.43: via ad glōriam proxima et quasi compendiāria (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From compendium, a saving; compendiāria (sc. via) is a short cut. Rare: Cicero has it once.
Traupman’s word for efficient. Classically of what is easy to handle (shoes, a sword) and of a person apt or nimble; habilitās is aptitude.

evidence: Cic. Top. 14 fin. (Lewis & Short, s.v. efficiō)
terms.comment: Classically “bringing about, producing”, the philosophers’ causa efficiēns; the sense “efficient” is Traupman’s. Cicero’s adverb efficienter (Fat. 34) is causal too.

phrases.latin: Gnāvus est; plūs ūnā hōrā cōnficit quam aliī tōtō diē.
phrases.english: He’s efficient; he gets more done in an hour than others in a whole day.

sources: Lewis & Short: navus · Lewis & Short: compendiarius · Lewis & Short: habilis · Lewis & Short: efficio
